topics.title: Chapter 12 — SSH and Remote Administration
topics.summary: Remote access is both a tool and a dependency. HarborWorks cannot safely harden SSH by removing its only working login method. The requirement is stronger: trusted operators must retain a verified path, unauthorized users must be rejected, and recovery must remain possible when the network path fails.

topics.title: 12.1 SSH Architecture
topics.summary: SSH establishes an encrypted connection, authenticates the server, authenticates the user, and carries channels such as an interactive terminal or file transfer. Server authentication and user authentication answer different questions. A user key proves something about the connecting user; a host key identifies the server being contacted.

topics.title: 12.4 Password Authentication
topics.summary: Password authentication sends proof through the encrypted SSH channel; it does not send the password as an unencrypted network login. Its risks include guessing, reuse, phishing, and stolen credentials. Rate controls and monitoring help, but they do not turn a weak shared password into accountable access.

blocks.text: Password authentication sends proof through the encrypted SSH channel; it does not send the password as an unencrypted network login. Its risks include guessing, reuse, phishing, and stolen credentials. Rate controls and monitoring help, but they do not turn a weak shared password into accountable access.

Password authentication is distinct from keyboard-interactive authentication, which may use PAM and multifactor prompts. Disabling one directive does not necessarily disable every password-like path. Conversely, disabling keyboard-interactive blindly can break an approved multifactor design. Test the effective policy for the actual account and source.
Linux example — 12.4

ssh -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o PubkeyAuthentication=no admin@web1

Keys need an owner, purpose, approval, rotation/revocation path, and protection. An untracked key in a shared account is not automatically safer operationally than a managed credential. Separate personal interactive keys from limited-purpose automation keys and remove authorization when its purpose ends.

topics.summary: For an ordinary non-FIPS lab where policy permits Ed25519, create a separate teaching key on admin1:

concepts.definition: For an ordinary non-FIPS lab where policy permits Ed25519, create a separate teaching key on admin1:

cards.question: Explain 12.6 Generating SSH Keys. What does the source establish?
cards.answer: For an ordinary non-FIPS lab where policy permits Ed25519, create a separate teaching key on admin1:

cards.question: What should you check after this section’s example?
cards.answer: Use a passphrase when prompted; protect the private file and share only the .pub file.

blocks.text: For an ordinary non-FIPS lab where policy permits Ed25519, create a separate teaching key on admin1:

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -a 64 \
  -f "$HOME/.ssh/harbor_lab" \
  -C 'harbor-lab-admin'
blocks.title: Original Linux example

blocks.text: Choose a passphrase interactively. Do not overwrite an existing key. Environments with approved cryptographic requirements may require a different supported algorithm, such as policy-approved RSA. The filename without .pub is private; the .pub file is the public half. Inspect the public fingerprint with ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/harbor_lab.pub.
Linux example — 12.6
Generate a fresh key without overwriting an existing one.

key="$HOME/.ssh/linux-lab_ed25519"
if [ -e "$key" ] || [ -e "$key.pub" ]; then printf 'Key path already exists; choose a new name\n'; else ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f "$key" -C linux-lab; fi

topics.title: 12.7 authorized_keys
topics.summary: The target account’s ~/.ssh/authorized_keys normally contains authorized public keys, one per line. Restrictive ownership and permissions prevent another user from altering access. A typical personal setup uses mode 700 for .ssh and 600 for authorized_keys, owned by the target account; parent directories must also satisfy the server’s checks.

Key lines can restrict behavior, including forwarding or permitted commands. Such restrictions are valuable for backups and automation, but a forced-command wrapper must safely validate inputs. Do not grant a general interactive root key merely because a scheduled task needs to read a particular directory. SELinux labeling can also affect access on enforcing systems.

topics.title: 12.9 Secure SSH Configuration
topics.summary: The safe order is establish console access, create a named administrator, install and verify a key, verify that administrator’s approved sudo rights, validate the server configuration, apply the change, and test a new session before closing the old one. Prefer accountable named accounts to routine direct root login.

blocks.text: scp provides a familiar source-to-destination file-copy interface over SSH. Modern OpenSSH versions normally use SFTP internally; legacy protocol behavior can differ in quoting and filename expansion. Inspect the installed manual rather than assuming shell wildcards behave identically across releases.

For a single explicitly named file, scp report.txt harbor-web1:report.txt copies into the target account’s home directory. Verify the host identity first, then compare the transferred file’s size or hash as appropriate. A successful copy is not a deployment: ownership, destination validation, activation, and rollback still need handling.

These categories lead to different tests.
